A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Continual GUI Agents work. Their complete main texts, equations, six tables, twelve figures and appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite substantial reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual GUI grounding experiments, reward and KL ablations, sensitivity analyses, and appendix experiments on joint training and reversed task order.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Tables 2–6 and the accompanying plots and visualization studies.

M1.justification: GUI-AiF retains the same APR-iF point-variance reward, ARR-iF Gaussian/Bhattacharyya separation reward, weighted combination and GRPO/KL training objective. Sections 3.1–3.3 disclose no algorithmic or architectural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Widget Captioning, ShowUI-web and OmniACT, and evaluate on ScreenSpot-V1, ScreenSpot-V2 and ScreenSpot-Pro. The domain and resolution scenarios and appendix visualization cases are unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in Tables 2–3 is identical. SeeClick, GUI-Actor, the combined SE-GUI† baseline and GUI-G2 remain in their corresponding comparisons, alongside the same proprietary and open-source reference models.

E3.justification: Both retain the same task sequences, accuracy metrics, Qwen2.5VL-3B backbone, one training epoch, learning rate 1e-6, batch size 8 and four predictions per instruction. The joint-training and reversed-order appendix protocols also match.

E4.justification: Both include the same reward-component and KL ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, forward-transfer evaluation, reward-behavior analysis and heatmap cases. Appendices A–D retain the joint-training comparison, reversed task order and text-versus-icon analysis without additional investigations.

E5.justification: The reward statistics and correlation reporting are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2–6 match exactly. For example, final GUI-AiF accuracies remain 81.7% and 83.5% on ScreenSpot-V1/V2 with GUI-G2, and 19.0% on ScreenSpot-Pro. The plotted findings and heatmap examples are also retained.

T1.justification: The sequential-task definitions and mathematical formulations in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations beyond the retained formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing continual GUI agents under domain/resolution shifts, proposing two anchoring rewards, and outperforming the reported baselines. The novelty and scientific scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning point exploration, scale adaptation, KL stabilization and text/OCR bias remain unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning the 3B model, restricted datasets and benchmarks, and unexplored layout, appearance and language shifts.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and GUI-AiF hyperlink to the abstract. However, the embedded target is github.com/your-username/ZoomUI, an apparent placeholder, so the PDFs do not establish usable code access. Other implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and related-work discussion match. The positioning against static GUI training and existing SFT/RFT approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds the code-access sentence, updates the preprint date and replaces the placeholder running header with the paper title. The substantive prose, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Document-wide retypesetting changes the fonts, heading and caption emphasis, table highlighting and placement of displays. Tables 2–3 occupy separate pages in v3, Table 6 moves alongside the appendix prose, and numerous figures are redistributed. The underlying table and figure content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves navigation and comparison through clearer heading hierarchy, a corrected running title and visible best-result highlighting in Tables 5–6. These are modest presentation gains; the scientific evidence is unchanged. The new code-availability statement points to an apparent placeholder, so it does not establish a reproducibility improvement.
